# I Built 5 Apps for 2 Hackathons in 4 Weeks And I realized we're living in the Personal Software era.

January 31, 2026

Steve Oak (Okkar Kyaw)

Prefer Audio Experience? Listen below 👇

After wrapping up the SOKK project where I explored RAG and knowledge graphs, I remember using Figma Make one night to speed up my frontend work. That got me thinking - how fast can I actually push out quality experiences while shipping solutions within constraints?

I wanted to ramp up even further. Test my limits. See what's possible when you combine curiosity with the right tools.

## Discovering the Hackathons

At the right time, I accidentally stumbled upon Craft Docs. They have **millions of users **worldwide, and they were running a winter hackathon with weekly winners. Around the same time, I saw YouWare (an SF startup building a vibe coding platform) was hosting their own challenge.

So I decided to join both. Just for fun.

## 1. Craftie Essence

A YouTube transcription and translation app that generates action lists, main points, and AI summaries. Works with or without bringing your own AI key (BYOK).

### What It Does

It's deeply integrated with Craft and built specifically for Craft users. No database needed. Everything stays local.

Feature |

What It Does

YouTube Transcription |

Pulls video transcripts automatically

Multi-language Translation |

Supports 40+ languages

AI Summary |

Generates TL;DR with streaming progress

Action Items |

Extracts tasks from video content

Prompt Mode |

Free tier - copy prompt to use in any AI

Auto Mode |

BYOK tier - direct processing with your API key

Craft Integration |

Posts directly to your Craft documents

### The "Achieve More" Insight

Here's something that clicked for me while building this. Everyone talks about AI helping us achieve the same with fewer resources. But what about achieving more with the same resources?

That question shaped how I approached this project.

### Heavy on Motion and Interaction

I focused on interactions, motions, and animations to see how fast I could create a complete visual experience. The whole app starts with a loading state. When you click, everything morphs into the app and the title flows into the hero section.

### The Win

Expecting nothing much but happy with the results and learnings, I got selected as a Complex Prize winner. The judges mentioned it was "fun and well-thought-through" and "extra fun and timely."

I used that prize money to invest more in keeping up with AI, agents, and advancements in design and development.

### Some Highlights

## The AI Tooling Journey

This period is where I explored and experimented way more than just Cursor and Claude. On top of working on these projects, I tried out:

Tool |

What I Learned

Factory Droid |

The "Infinite Context Engine" - sounds like marketing, but the hype matched the experience. Never had to worry about memory or context. Ranked #1 in terminal benchmarks.

WARP Terminal |

Modern terminal experience, good vibes

GLM 4.6-4.7 |

Chinese LLM (Affordable Claude alternative)

Gemini |

Multimodal generation and understanding

Codex |

Deep analysis capabilities

People kept recommending Factory Droid. The infinite context thing intrigued me most. It delivered.

But as I'm writing this case study in January 2026, I've switched back to Claude Code. It now supports MCP search tools, has a Chrome Extension, and Interview Mode. I still don't understand why other CLI competitors aren't implementing these features when they already have the foundations. When I use other tools, I have to use my own interview MCP tool which I'll share with everyone later.

## 2. Craftie Clarity

A hybrid Calendar and Kanban app for Craft. Nothing groundbreaking on paper, but it was one of the most requested features by Craft users. I'd been wanting to build something like this since I started using Notion back in 2019.

### What It Does

Feature |

Description

Calendar View |

Full schedule view with a gold accent theme

Kanban Board |

Drag-and-drop task columns

Tab Switching |

Horizontal camera-pan transitions between views

Daily Brief |

Quick view popover from the bottom nav

Collection Filter |

Filter tasks by Craft collection

The tab switching uses horizontal camera-pan transitions. When you switch from Calendar to Board, it feels like the camera is panning across a physical space. Small detail, but it makes navigation feel spatial rather than just swapping screens.

This project later became the foundation for YouSoul.

## 3. Craftie Import Extension

A web clipper with media snapshot features and AI-assisted extraction.

### Why Extensions?

This is where I got the idea about developing extensions. You've got more control and freedom with extensions, plus widespread access compared to standalone apps. So I decided to try building something useful for Craft users.

### The Signal-Based Approach

Most web clippers route content based on what type of page you're on - recipe pages get the recipe handler, event pages get the event handler. But that breaks when content doesn't fit neat categories.

I took a different approach: signal-based extraction.

Instead of asking "what type of page is this?", I ask "what signals does this page have?" Then the user picks where it goes:

Destination |

What It Does

Document |

Full content with formatting

Daily Note |

Quick capture to today's note

Task |

Action item with optional schedule

Collection |

Schema-driven structured data

## 4. Craftie Mail

Gmail to Craft Tasks & Daily Notes integration with AI insights. Also tailored specifically for Craft users.

### The Three AI Modes

Mode |, How It Works |, Cost, MCP Prompt |

App generates prompt → paste in Claude with Craft MCP → AI creates tasks directly |

Free

Manual Prompt |

Copy prompt → paste in any AI → copy response → paste back |

Free

Auto BYOK |

One-click processing with your API key |

~$0.01/use

### The Commitment Tracker

Here's what makes it different from other email-to-task apps: it scans your SENT emails for promises you made.

Most tools look at received emails for things others want you to do. What about "I'll send that by Friday" or "Let me follow up next week"? Those commitments get lost.

Same pattern that Discord Coach used to win a Grand Prize in an earlier hackathon. "What did I promise?" is a different question than "What do I need to do?"

## 5. YouSoul Vibe Productivity System

This was for a different hackathon, YouWare, the vibe coding platform. I downloaded the foundation from Craftie Clarity, used Claude Code mostly for development, did some workarounds, and hosted it there.

### Why Build This?

I've been wanting to create agentic features for productivity for a while. Now there are agentic features in Notion, Gemini, and others. But most are just GPT-wrapped chats. That's not enough anymore.

So I built this to be importable from any other platform, with all the Calendar and Kanban features you'd expect.

The key difference from other AI productivity tools: event-based sync that actually updates the UI in real-time when AI creates or modifies tasks. Plus mood correlation and pattern insights across 73 designed features.

## The Bigger Picture

Now I built all of these in just 4 weeks during my free time.

What does that mean?

We can build almost everything we have in mind now. Productivity and speed have gone through the roof. Human curiosity and innovation keep surprising me.

There's always paid and open source projects and updates popping up almost every day.

For example, as I write this, Clawdbot/MoltBot/OpenClaw is the most trending tool. I bought a Mac Mini to boost my productivity and already have workflows running for my personal and professional life.

### On Energy Usage

Everything has pros and cons. People are complaining about AI causing energy usage spikes and hardware demand. But I'm on the positive side. I think we'll figure it out somehow. We always do.

## The Personal Software Era

Think about this: history repeats for the better.

Back in the days, only big companies had those expensive computers. Then the PC era came. Everyone could afford a computer and enjoy their potential.

Now it's time for PS: personal software.

People are already creating their own daily life apps and systems for themselves, their friends, and small groups.

This is our moment!

# Vibe coding won't make your product stand out. Here's what will + CASE STUDY

January 17, 2026

Steve Oak (Okkar Kyaw)

TLDR

Maryam, an Apple engineer, had a generic Next.js site for her matcha community (MBM). We rebuilt it using the hierarchy that works: Framer (specialized platform) + AI (leverage on top). Result: Immediate trust perception, actual brand deals, and a site people praise. This case study breaks down the exact process.

Prefer Audio Experience? Listen below 👇

You're paying for AI. $20/month, maybe $200. Of course you want it to be magic.

That's the trap. You paid money, so your brain wants results. You want to describe what you want and have it appear, perfect, ready to ship. Like a genie.

But here's what actually happens: you slowly accept "good enough." You keep prompting, keep iterating, keep spending tokens. Before you know it, your product looks like everyone else's product. You became a boiling frog and didn't notice.

The ones who stand out in 2026 accepted a different reality. AI is leverage, not a magic pill.

## The Slopidemic

"AI Slop" was Word of the Year 2025. Merriam-Webster and the American Dialect Society both picked it.

Everyone has access to the same tools. v0, lovable, bolt, cursor, gemini, claude, you name it. All producing similar outputs when used the default way. 82% of AI-generated sites/apps share the same layouts. Same onboarding flows. Same card-based UIs. Same everything.

When your product looks like everyone else's, you're invisible. 1.2% conversion rate for generic AI output vs 2.8% for custom work. That's 2.3x worse. Brand recall drops 25% when there's nothing distinctive to remember.

55% of consumers feel uncomfortable when they sense AI was behind the marketing. Not because AI is bad. Because they can tell nobody cared enough to make it unique.

If you're shipping slop, you're cooked.

## The hierarchy that works

Stop expecting AI to be the genie. Start with specialized solutions first.

1. Expert, agency, or team Hire someone who understands both design and development. Someone who knows what distinctive looks like in your market. Still the gold standard.

2. Specialized platforms Find tools built by people who understand your specific craft. Not generic AI builders, but platforms where the craft comes first and AI assists.

My picks: Framer for websites, Figma for design. Claude for coding. Find yours for your domain.

3. AI as leverage on top Now add AI. Not as the genie that does everything. As the multiplier that accelerates what you're already doing.

Most people reverse this. They start with generic AI tools, hope for magic, get slop.

The question isn't whether to use AI. It's 2026. Everyone uses AI. The question is: are you using it to do the same thing as everyone else, or to multiply your edge?

## MBM Case Study

Maryam is an Apple software engineer building a matcha community called MBM (Matcha by Maryam). Events, content, products, partnerships across the US and Canada.

She had a Next.js site she built "just to share" her matcha journey. Functional but generic. Looked like any other hobby blog. No time to make it special. Work at Apple, sourcing matcha from Japan, planning events. Something had to give.

Problem: when you're pitching to brands, your website IS your credibility. Generic website means generic perception.

She could have kept prompting AI tools. Kept hoping for the genie. That's the boiling frog trap.

What we did instead: specialized solution + AI leverage.

First, strategy questions. What should visitors feel? What makes MBM different from other matcha content? What patterns are competitors overdoing?

Then Figma/Gemini prototyping. Built with Framer. AI for speed and iteration. Human direction for differentiation.

The before: generic site, could have been any matcha blog.

The after:

- Instant welcoming and memorable EXPERIENCE for target audience
- The right green that felt like nature, growth, freshness.
- Minimal motion. Enough to feel alive and premium, not gimmicky.
- Copy speaking directly to matcha lovers. Inside jokes. The feeling of belonging.

Result: people praise her. They trust her more to do deals. The website became an asset, not just a checkbox. +65% trust boost with human refinement is real.

That's what happens when you stop hoping for the genie and start using the hierarchy. Check out the site here.

P.S. We also extended to brochures, Luma-inspired app designs, React Native prototypes. AI accelerated all of it. But the manual craft came first.

## The multiplier

Most people use AI to reduce effort. Same output, less work.

Flip it.

Use AI to multiply output. Same effort, more results.

SPEED × QUALITY × VOLUME

Not additive. Multiplicative.

10x iterations. 10x experiments. 10x directions explored. That's where distinctive comes from. Not from one magic prompt, but from the volume of attempts with human direction.

## Closing

Accept reality. Think different. Act different.

When everyone uses the same tools the same way, the ones who stand out are the ones who refused to settle for the default output.
